name: Mommotti
body:
Mommotti
CR 4

This creature resembles a bald, hairless human with a muscular frame and a featureless face, every inch of its surface smooth and black. Glowing red eyes flicker and disappear in that fearsome visage. It carries a sack of the same black material as its skin.

XP 1,200
LE Medium outsider (evil, extraplanar, kyton, lawful)
Init +2; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +9; Aura darkness aura

DEFENSE

AC 13, touch 12, flat-footed 11 (+2 Dex, +1 natural)
hp 37 (4d10+12)
Fort +8, Ref +3, Will +8
Defensive Abilities blend with shadows DR 5/silver or good; Immune cold; SR 15; Weaknesses light blindness, vulnerability to fire

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee 2 claw +8 (1d6+4 plus grab), kidnap sack +8 (1d8+6)
Special Attacks kidnap sack, unnerving gaze (20 ft., DC 15)

STATISTICS

Str 19, Dex 14, Con 18, Int 11, Wis 14, Cha 16
Base Atk +4; CMB +8 (+12 to grappling); CMD 20
Feats Iron Will, Skill Focus (Intimidate)
Skills Acrobatics +9, Bluff +10, Intimidate +13, Perception +9, Sense Motive +9, Stealth +9
Languages Common, Infernal
SQ shadow slip

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Blend with Shadows (Ex)

While in an area with dim light or darkness, a mommotti always gains the benefit of concealment.

Darkness Aura (Ex)

A mommotti is surrounded by an aura of darkness (as the spell). Creatures without darkvision can spot the mommotti’s location by its red eyes that flare to light when it attacks.

Kidnap Sack (Ex)

When a mommotti starts its turn with a Small or Medium sized opponent grappled, it can attempt a new combat maneuver check (as though attempting to pin the opponent). If it succeeds, it deals claw damage and shoves its prey into the sack.

The kidnapped creature keeps the grappled condition while the mommotti does not. Attacks against the sack are resolved as if made against the mommotti itself. If the sack takes 15 or more damage from a single source of damage, a hole is made, allowing the creature inside to escape by falling prone within 5 feet of the mommotti. The sack becomes mundane upon the mommottis death.

A full sack can be used as a two-handed bludgeoning weapon causing equal damage to both the opponent hit and inside the sack.

Shadow Slip (Su)

As a move action, the mommotti briefly slips through the Shadow Plane, reappearing up to 30 feet away. That the starting point and destination must be in darkness or dim light.

Unnerving Gaze (Su)

A creature within 20 feet that can see the mommotti’s glowing red eyes perceives its deepest fears of what lurks in the dark, becoming shaken for 1 minute (DC 15 Will negates). A creature succeeding on the save is immune to that mommotti’s gaze for 24 hours. This is a mind-affecting fear effect.

The save is DC is Charisma-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary, pair, or ring (3-6)
Treasure standard

Quiet, menacing figures, the mommotti are wicked fiends that stalk the night in search of victims. A mommotti’s flesh is dark as the surrounding night, with red eyes glowing faintly from its face. A bulging sack slung over one broad shoulder seems to shift and move, as if it holds something alive. Cruel beings, they prefer to prey on the weak and fearful, those smaller than themselves and those who cannot fight back.

The fate of a mommotti’s victims is always terrible. Some are simply eaten. Others are traded or sold to other horrible creatures. Mommotti often work for hags or other fiends, kidnapping folk at their behest. Whatever their fate, those stolen by a mommotti are never seen again.

Mommotti enjoy scaring their prey. They take great pleasure in the fear of others. When a mommotti fails to capture its intended victim, it is often because the fiend takes too much time indulging itself in terrifying the victim, allowing time for the victim to escape or for help to arrive.

The mommotti is a bogeyman figure, often mentioned by parents as a way to scare children into behaving. (“Go to sleep! If you stay up past your bedtime, the mommotti is sure to come and steal you away!”) A mommotti that hears such things is sure to take the scolded child, as they revel in the grief experienced by such parents when their children go missing, as if they had summoned the thing itself, and blame themselves for the loss.
